title: Public Internet, mobile networks and global reach

paras: Technology, infrastructure, network architecture, institutional ownership and business economics.
Commercial ISPs, DNS, BGP, IXPs, fiber backbones, submarine cables, GSM/3G/4G, Wi-Fi, CDNs, data centers, HTTPS and broadband access.

blocks.h2: Who developed, funded, owned and operated the systems?
paras: National regulators, private and state-owned carriers, ISPs, submarine cable consortia, ICANN ecosystem, standards bodies, enterprises and consumers. These participants had different roles: research sponsorship, equipment supply, network operation, regulation, standardization and service consumption should not be conflated.
Last-mile access joins ISP/mobile-core networks; autonomous systems exchange routes through peering and transit; CDNs cache near customers.
Internet subscriptions, roaming, peering/transit contracts, hosting, e-commerce, advertising and mobile data plans.
Public Internet is a network of networks; privately owned access networks may offer public service, while government networks may remain restricted.

A mobile user opens a banking app: radio access connects to a carrier core, DNS locates a service, routing reaches an origin or CDN, TLS protects the session, and bank systems authenticate and process requests.
A carrier can own the last mile, another company the transit network, a consortium the submarine cable, and a cloud provider the application infrastructure.
